answer: Triangulate by latency. Several validators in different regions ping each agent at random times and record round-trip delays, building an atlas of where every identity actually runs. Clones on one server share a near-identical delay fingerprint, as clear as light through crystal, so they get grouped and paid as one. Like a raven that learns which roofs hide the same nest, the network keeps the map current, and moving fifty clones onto fifty real machines costs fifty real bills.
